newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent up on Venezuela, N. Sea wets inactive.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent up on Venezuela, N. Sea wets inactive.

text.p: Cash Brent firmed on Tuesday afternoon, lifted by news that Venezuela's main oil export shipping channel had been blocked, but other North Sea markets were inactive, traders said.
"The Venezuela story lifted outright levels and also pulled the spreads up," said a trader.
A dredger went aground in the Lake Maracaibo shipping lane on Monday night, shutting the channel to tankers which normally export more than one million barrels of crude per day.
Oct Brent on the IPE put on 24 cents to $19.17 a barrel by 1552 GMT and intermonth cash spreads also firmed after drifting lower in early talk.
Sept/Oct and Oct/Nov were both pegged around -9/-6 cents, three or four cents firmer over the day.
The firmer Brent cash curve was also reflected in short-term swaps, with next week's (Aug 25-29) CFDs bid at -28 cents below October, two cents above early levels.
Dated Brent, however, remained under pressure with two end-August cargoes still unsold but other North Sea grades were solid in very quiet business, traders said.
"I have nothing to report. Nothing has been done," said a major seller of North Sea crudes.
The Aug 28-30 and Aug 29-31 Brent cargoes were last heard offered at 35 cents below October, well below the last Brent deal at September -15 cents on Friday.
Best bids heard on Monday were around September -35 cents.
Brent's weakness was underlined when two September dates turning wet on Monday were five o'clocked.
At least one of the two Sept 2-4 cargoes was deferred to Tuesday, the other holder was undecided and another date, Sept 3-5, turns wet today.
